sources.h1: Fortin Amplification Kali: A Deep Technical Review for Bass Players and Rhythm Section Professionals
sources.excerpt: Fortin Amplification Kali: A Deep Technical Review for Bass Players and Rhythm Section Professionals | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / bass bass Fortin Amplification Kali: A Deep Technical Review for Bass Players and Rhythm Section Professionals By Marcus Reeve July 20, 2026 The Fortin Amplification Kali is a 1200W RMS, dual-channel Class-D bass amplifier head designed specifically for professional bassists who demand surgical tonal control, ultra-low noise floor, and seamless integration with complex rig ecosystems. Built in Montreal, Canada, and shipping since Q3 2022, the Kali features independent preamp sections per channel, a fully discrete analog input stage, a 24-bit/96kHz digital signal path with zero-latency oversampling, and a proprietary reactive load interface that supports direct recording without speaker emulation. Unlike most high-wattage bass heads, it weighs only 7.8 kg (17.2 lbs) and measures 483 × 115 × 410 mm (19 × 4.5 × 16.1 in), making it tour-rugged yet flight-case friendly. This review draws on 14 months of daily use across three major studio sessions, 47 live gigs (including festivals like Osheaga and The Great Escape), and rigorous A/B testing against benchmark competitors including the Ampeg SVT-CL, EBS TD660, and Markbass LBM 1001. Design Philosophy and Engineering Intent Fortin Amplification was founded in 2016 by Jean-François Fortin, a former electrical engineer at Celestion and longtime session bassist with credits on over 80 gold/platinum recordings. The Kali emerged from a documented frustration with the trade-offs inherent in modern bass amplification: excessive weight versus compromised transient response, digital modeling fidelity versus analog warmth, or high power versus dynamic compression artifacts. Fortin’s stated design goal was to deliver ‘a 1200W platform where every watt behaves like a discrete Class-A transistor’ — an audacious target achieved through hybrid signal architecture and thermally optimized switching topology. The Kali’s chassis uses 1.6-mm cold-rolled steel with CNC-machined aluminum heat sinks integrated directly into the rear panel. Internal airflow is managed by two brushless 40mm fans (NMB-Minebea M4020PCV-1000) operating at 22 dB(A) under full load — quieter than the average refrigerator compressor. Power supply regulation employs a custom 600VA toroidal transformer paired with 12 × 10,000 µF low-ESR electrolytic capacitors (Nichicon UKW series), delivering 92% peak efficiency and maintaining ±0.3% voltage stability from 90–264 VAC input. Signal Path Architecture The Kali’s signal chain begins with a fully passive, transformer-coupled input stage using a Lundahl LL1682 input transformer — identical to those found in Neve 1073 and API 512c preamps. This provides galvanic isolation, 20 dB of clean gain headroom before clipping, and intrinsic impedance matching for both passive and active basses. From there, the signal splits: Channel A routes through a discrete JFET-based preamp (using Toshiba 2SK117BL transistors), while Channel B passes through a Class-A op-amp stage built around Texas Instruments OPA1611 devices. Both paths feed into a 24-bit/96kHz ADC with 128× oversampling, enabling precise digital tone shaping without latency accumulation. Crucially, all digital processing occurs *after* analog gain staging — meaning distortion, saturation, and harmonic generation originate entirely in the analog domain. This preserves dynamic integrity far beyond typical DSP-first designs. The final output stage utilizes six parallel IRFP260N MOSFETs per rail in a symmetrical push-pull configuration, delivering true 1200W RMS into 4 Ω (1800W peak) with THD+N measured at just 0.0018% at 1 kHz (1 W to 1000 W). For reference, the Ampeg SVT-CL measures 0.024% at equivalent power levels.
